comparison: Perfect agreement on core behavioral findings (C1, C19-C21, C54-C55). Both evaluations find the fundamental demonstration of differential feeding on familiar vs novel bacteria to be well-supported. Reviewers described work as 'thorough, interesting, and novel' without challenging these claims.

Disagreement on ADF activation and serotonin release claims (C2, C42-C43, C45-C46). OpenEval finds calcium imaging and immunohistochemistry data sufficient, while peer reviewers raised significant methodological concerns about calcium imaging study quality, baseline ratios, bleaching rates, and experimental timing, creating uncertainty.

Disagreement on serotonin signaling mechanism (C22-C25, C28 overlap). OpenEval finds pharmacological and genetic evidence sufficient. Peer reviewers expressed concern about 'negative conclusions from experiments that have control pumping rates on the very low side' (Figures 4b, 5a), questioning whether low baseline rates undermine conclusions about mutant phenotypes.

Disagreement on ADF-specific role claims (C3, C32-C35). OpenEval finds genetic rescue and ablation experiments convincing. Peer reviewers specifically flagged concerns about 'negative conclusions' from NSM ablation experiments (Figure 8c-d) with low baseline pumping rates, creating uncertainty about whether NSM truly does not contribute.

Disagreement on humoral signaling mechanism (C4-C5, C36-C41). OpenEval finds cell-specific rescue experiments and genetic evidence strongly supportive. Peer reviewers asked critical question 'Is it possible to elicit pharyngeal pumping by ADF activation?' suggesting the proposed pathway's sufficiency remains incompletely validated without direct demonstration.

Agreement on antagonistic pathway model (C6, C47-C51). Both evaluations support the conditioned media experiments and model of antagonistic regulation by familiar vs novel bacterial cues. Peer reviewers did not challenge these findings or the logical framework.

Disagreement on baseline bacterial strain differences (C75-C79 vs C76-C79). OpenEval finds these control data statistically supported. Peer reviewers expressed major concern that 'day-to-day variations in feeding rates are as large or larger than the familiarity effect' (100 vs 20 pumps/min), questioning reliability of strain comparisons and data combination methodology.

Agreement on inhibitory serotonin signaling characterization (C73-C74 overlap with C26-C27, C29-C30). Both evaluations support claims about opposing receptor functions and triple mutant phenotype. Peer reviewers did not raise specific concerns about these characterizations.

Partial overlap on serotonin receptor claims (C26-C27, C29-C30). OpenEval finds systematic receptor analysis convincing. Peer review uncertainty about low baseline pumping rates in mutant experiments (R3) extends to interpretation of receptor-specific effects, though reviewers did not directly challenge the receptor characterization claims.

OpenEval evaluated background knowledge claims (C7-C15) about food choice and neophobia as well-supported by literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not comment on these contextual/definitional claims.

OpenEval evaluated C. elegans model justification claims (C16-C18) as supported by established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not challenge the choice of model organism.

OpenEval evaluated extensive background neurobiology claims (C31, C44, C60-C72) as appropriately cited and accurate. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not comment on these established knowledge claims.
OpenEval marked preliminary 24-hour memory data (C52) as uncertain due to lack of shown data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not comment on this claim.

OpenEval evaluated ADF's role in other learning forms (C53, C57-C58) as supported by prior literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not comment on these contextual claims.

OpenEval marked speculative/predictive claims (C56, C59, C62, C64) as uncertain, requiring additional experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not explicitly address these forward-looking hypotheses.
